newsitem.title: RUSSIA: High demand seen for Russian tax-liable T-bills.
newsitem.headline: High demand seen for Russian tax-liable T-bills.

text.p: Non-resident demand for new tax-liable Russian Treasury bills will keep prices low at Wednesday's auction, preserving a 3-4 percent spread over non tax-liable government securities, dealers said on Tuesday.
* Dealers forecast yields on 4.50 trillion roubles of 196-day T-bills (series 22071) liable for the 15 percent profits tax would be 29.49-35.42 percent.
* They forecast yields on 7.00 trillion roubles of 287-day T-bills (series 22072) liable for the tax would be 30.59-36.02 percent.
(One of 12 dealers surveyed forecast yields for both issues five percentage points higher than the rest.)
* Tax-liable series 22069 T-bills maturing July 16 yielded 30.54 percent at close of the market on Tuesday.
* Tax-liable series 22070 T-bills maturing November 19 yielded 31.06 percent at close of the market on Tuesday.
* Average yield on the secondary market fell to 28.3 percent from 29.9 percent
* Turnover rose to 4.56 trillion roubles from 3.46 trillion roubles.

Dealers said prices for issues liable for 15 percent profits tax rose in trade on Tuesday and that demand for roubles to buy treasury bills had kept overnight rates at 40 percent until evening, when they eased to 25 percent.
"You only have to look at the overnight rate to see that it is not worth waiting for a premium at the auction," said Renaissance Capital dealer Alexei Orekhov.
Non-residents bought about 30 percent of tax-liable issues at last week's auction, according to official data.
